reviewBasis.reviewRule: Compare both pinned candidates; propose an exact candidate only when one meaning is defensible for the grade/POS intent. Otherwise preserve unresolved or request candidate/POS relevance review.

entries.reason: Event-preclusion and stopping an entity from acting or remaining in a state are both ordinary readings.
The meal reading is the ordinary child-facing noun; the event/party reading is secondary.
Feeling pride or being a reason for pride is the ordinary child-facing adjective; the lofty/majestic reading is secondary.
The candidates split transitive make-better from intransitive get-better; a bare verb supplies no argument structure.
The unintended harmful/mishap reading is the ordinary child-facing noun; the chance/fortuity reading is secondary.
The legislative-body reading is the primary civic meaning for children; the alternate named/event reading is not the intended general-vocabulary sense.
A commitment to do or not do something is the ordinary child-facing noun; future potential is a distinct secondary reading.
A day of observance and a period away from work/school are both ordinary child-facing readings.
Talking something over and treating a topic in speech/writing are both ordinary classroom uses.
Natural ability or aptitude is the ordinary child-facing meaning; a talented person/group is secondary metonymy.
Having the ability or power to create is the ordinary classroom adjective; the specialized causal/constructive reading is secondary.
A class/group whose members share attributes is the ordinary school meaning; the abstract philosophical category reading is secondary.
Having or showing knowledge and skill is the ordinary adjective used with people/work; the alternate specialized relation reading is secondary.
A person harmed by an event or action is the ordinary child-facing meaning; ritual-sacrifice usage is secondary.
Preferred-above-others and broadly favored/appealing readings are both plausible without a phrase or referent.
Food grain and rice plant are both primary-school meanings, especially across Food and Plants topics.
Bath/shower room and toilet/restroom readings are both ordinary and region-sensitive.
Emotional tranquility and absence of wind/disturbance are both ordinary noun readings.
The state or fact of existing is the general meaning; the totality/way-of-life reading is more specialized.
The pedal bicycle reading is the ordinary primary-school noun; motorcycle usage is a secondary colloquial reading.
The queue source is verb-only, while the ordinary child-vocabulary lemma is the noun clothing item; do not resolve the verb candidates without confirming intended POS.
Seeing an event happen and formally being present/attesting overlap without sentence context.
A charge paid for a service or privilege is the ordinary child-facing noun; the property-law estate reading is specialized.
The food made from milk is the ordinary child-facing noun; slang/other specialized uses are secondary.
Mother/father and biological progenitor organism are both primary-school meanings across family and science contexts.
Conforming closely to fact or a standard is the ordinary classroom adjective; specialized performance readings are secondary.
Relating to chemistry and involving/produced by chemical substances or processes are both plausible science readings.
A narrow road/path and a marked strip for traffic or racing are both ordinary child-facing meanings.
Lasting or intended to last is the ordinary classroom adjective; specialized non-temporary/status readings are secondary.
Dissimilarity and inequality/not-the-same readings are too close to select exactly from the bare adjective.
Electromagnetic radiation and the resulting radiographic image are both common primary-school science/health meanings.
The baked food is the ordinary child-facing noun; money slang is secondary.
Approval or consent to do something is the ordinary child-facing meaning; a formal authorization/document reading is secondary.
Inherited beliefs/customs and a specific long-standing practice are both ordinary child-facing uses.
Historically important and belonging/relating to notable past history are close enough to need usage context.
The sport and the ball used to play it are both ordinary child-facing noun referents.
The quality of being important or significant is the ordinary classroom meaning; rank/status importance is secondary.
The people employed by an organization is the general meaning; the personnel/HR department reading is secondary.
An organized competition is the ordinary modern child-facing meaning; the historical jousting tournament is secondary.
The legal act of taking someone into custody is the ordinary social/civic noun; stoppage/medical arrest is a distinct secondary reading.
